description: We are MINEIRØ, a team passionate about technology, science, music, and innovation. We aim to connect people with our planet through NASA data, AI, sound, and accessibility. We are looking for creative and curious people with skills in software development, music production, data science, AI, or UI/UX who want to collaborate, learn, and build something meaningful together.
summary:
NASA's Earth and climate visualizations rely almost exclusively on sight, limiting access for visually impaired people. With that in mind, we built MINEIRØ - The Earth Experience: an accessible, multi-sensory projected room and live 3D web simulator that lets users hear and explore NASA data in real time.

Using only two projectors and one screen-reader-ready device (or any web browser via our online 3D simulator), visitors launch a guided space mission with bilingual neural voice narration and 3-point 8D spatial audio. Once in orbit, our engine samples RGB pixels and spatial coordinates from five official NASA SVS datasets (lightning, temperature, wind, CO, and NOx), translating each layer into distinct Web Audio instruments.

Why it matters: MINEIRØ makes complex climate science more inclusive for blind and low-vision explorers while enabling anyone in the world to create an accessible, large-scale NASA immersion.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

MINEIRØ - The Earth Experience transforms real NASA Earth observation data into a multi-sensory, accessible experience where blind, low-vision, and sighted explorers can hear and interact with planetary science in real time.

Our engine samples RGB pixel values, scientific colorbars, and geographic coordinates from five official NASA SVS datasets and translates them live through the Web Audio API:

- Lightning (SVS 5011): drives crystalline melodic notes with 8D spatial panning;

- Carbon Monoxide (SVS 5153): generates harmonic chord pads;

- Air Temperature (SVS 5147): controls musical tempo (BPM) and thermal pulse;

- Nitrogen Oxides (SVS 5154): shapes sub-harmonic bass lines;

- Near-Surface Wind (SVS 5148): synthesizes stereo airflow textures.

Why It Matters & Intended Impact:

Climate and space imagery usually depend on sight alone. MINEIRØ makes NASA data audible and navigable for visually impaired users through a screen-reader-ready tablet controller, high-contrast WCAG AAA mode, and bilingual neural voice narration (English and Brazilian Portuguese). Just as importantly, it is radically accessible to set up: requiring only two projectors and one controlling device (or any web browser via our online 3D simulator), anyone in the world can create a giant, inclusive NASA immersion.

Creativity & User Journey:

Rather than a static dashboard, MINEIRØ guides visitors through an interactive space mission across three projected surfaces (Left Wall, Right Wall, and Ceiling):

1. Mission Briefing & Boarding: An animated 3D astronaut guide (MINEIRØ) invites the visitor aboard while metallic blast doors seal the cabin, revealing a launch field porthole on the left wall and the rocket nosecone on the ceiling with spatial pneumatic audio.

2. 8D Liftoff & Zero Gravity: A 5-to-1 countdown triggers 3-point 8D thruster propulsion. In orbit, the ceiling opens to reveal deep space and passing meteors before the cabin dissolves into the 3D Earth globe and floating country flags.

3. Live Planetary Mixer: Visitors select countries and toggle the five NASA visual/audio layers individually like a Photoshop-style mixer.

4. Gamified Return: Ending the mission brings Earth closer and awards a mission recognition medal.

Tools, Software & Hardware:

- Software & Stack: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, Web Audio API, Motion (motion/react), topojson-client / world-atlas (Natural Earth cartography), Vitest (39 automated unit tests).

- Neural Audio & Accessibility: @mintplex-labs/piper-tts-web (ONNX Runtime Web with OPFS caching) and Web Speech API fallback.

- Hardware Setup: 2 projectors (L-corner wall + ceiling) + 1 tablet/device + 3-point stereo/8D speaker setup (or 100% browser-based 3D Room Simulator).

Factors Considered & SI Transparency:

We prioritized WCAG AAA accessibility, corner-pin homography calibration for real room walls, zero-latency fallback audio, and bilingual support. In accordance with NASA Space Apps SI guidelines, we acknowledge the use of Piper TTS neural voices (en_US-bryce-medium and pt_BR-faber-medium) for accessible narration, AI coding assistants with specialized engineering/design skills to accelerate code refactoring and testing, and AI-assisted generation for the decorative Earth horizon illustration on the entry portal. All system architecture, NASA SVS data-to-audio mapping, and final verification were directed and authored by our team.
